dr収集日: The day garbage is collected. Put your garbage out at the designated place on that day.
dr開栓: Turning on the gas so you can use it. A staff member often visits your home.
dr立ち会い: Being there while a staff member does work. You or someone for you waits at home.
dr都市ガス: A type of gas that comes to homes through pipes.
drプロパンガス: A type of gas. Also called LP gas.
drガスコンロ: A cooking appliance that uses a gas flame. It must match your type of gas.
dr口座振替: Automatic payment from your bank account. You submit an application form.
drお客さまセンター: The part of a company that handles customer calls and questions.
drお客さま番号: Your number from the company. It is on bills and meter reading slips. Give it when you call.
dr検針票: A paper showing how much gas, electricity, or water you used.
dr使用期間: The period of use: from when to when you used it.
dr使用量: How much gas, etc. you used.
dr再発行: Having a document made and issued again.
dr在庫: Goods a store has for sale. They may be in the back even if not on the shelf.
dr試着: Putting on clothes before buying. Ask a staff member first.
drお取り寄せ: Having an item the store doesn't have sent from another store, etc.
dr切らしております: A polite way of saying the store doesn't have that item now.
drサービスカウンター: The place in a store for returns, exchanges, and questions.
dr返品: Giving an item back to the store and getting your money back.
dr交換: Swapping an item you bought for another one of the same item.
dr粗大ごみ: Large garbage such as furniture. You usually apply by phone or online to put it out.
dr処理券: A sticker you buy and attach to oversized garbage. Often sold at convenience stores.
dr家電リサイクル: Rules for disposing of air conditioners, TVs, refrigerators, washing machines, etc. They cannot go out as oversized garbage. Ask the store where you bought them.
dr冷蔵庫: An electric box that keeps food and drinks cold.
dr受付センター: A place that takes applications by phone or online.
dr予約: Arranging a day and time in advance.
dr満席: All seats are taken; no seats are free.
drコース: A set of dishes served in a fixed order at a restaurant.
drお席: A polite word for "seat"; a place to sit.
dr名様: A polite way to say "people". "2名様" means "2 people".
drお迎え: A car coming to where you are.
dr目印: Something easy to see that shows where a place is, such as a nearby shop or building.
dr予約料: A fee that may be charged when you book a taxi to pick you up.
dr初診: Seeing a doctor at a hospital for the first time.
dr保険証: A card showing you have medical insurance. Show it at hospital reception.
drマイナンバーカード: A card with your personal number. It can sometimes be used instead of a health insurance card at hospitals.
drせき: Air forced out hard from the throat. Common with colds.
dr問診票: A form about your symptoms, when they started, medicines you take, etc. Fill it in before seeing the doctor.
dr返金: A store giving back the money for something you bought. If you paid by card, it usually goes back to the card.
drレシート: A paper from the store listing what you bought and the prices. Show it for exchanges.
dr初期不良: A product that is broken or doesn't work right just after you buy it.
drコードレス掃除機: A vacuum cleaner without a power cord. It runs on a charged battery.
dr取り寄せ: Having an item the store doesn't have sent from another store or company. You wait until it arrives.
dr何名様: Means "How many in your party?" Answer with the number, e.g. "3 people", or show with your fingers.
dr禁煙席: A seat where smoking is not allowed.
dr喫煙席: A seat where smoking is allowed. People under the legal smoking age cannot enter.
dr全席禁煙: Smoking is not allowed at any seat in the restaurant.
dr喫煙室: A room for smoking. In some restaurants, this is the only place you can smoke.
drテーブル席: A regular seat at a table with chairs.
drカウンター席: Seats in a row at a long counter in front of where the staff work.
drお子様用のいす: A special chair for small children.
dr照り焼き: Food grilled with a sweet sauce made from soy sauce, mirin, etc.
dr塩焼き: Food grilled with salt. Often fish.
dr定食: A set of rice, miso soup, side dishes, etc.
drみりん: A sweet seasoning for cooking. It contains alcohol.
drゼラチン: Something that sets jelly, etc. It may be made from pigs or other animals.
drだし: A soup base made by simmering fish, kelp, meat, etc. Used to flavor food.
pj81: Support System for Self-Reliance of Needy Persons
A system where your local city office works with you to help if you are struggling to live (no money, no job, or no place to live).
pj82: Money paid to the national government, prefecture, city, ward, etc.
pj83: A hospital department that treats bones, joints, muscles, etc.
pj84: A certificate booklet issued by your local city office to people with a mental disability that makes daily life difficult.
pj85: An agreement between countries about taxes. People from countries with a treaty with Japan may pay less tax.
pj86: A person enrolled only in the National Pension, such as self-employed people with their own shop, farmers, fishers, and people who are not working.
pj87: A person whose spouse is enrolled in Employees' Pension Insurance and is under 65, and whose own yearly income is less than 1.3 million yen. Enrolled only in the National Pension.
pj88: A document you give to your company when you quit, stating your reason, etc.
pj89: A person enrolled in both the National Pension and Employees' Pension Insurance, such as people working at companies, factories, or shops.
pj90: Money that people who leave the Japanese pension system and return to their home country can receive.
pj91: Part-time workers and others who work fewer hours than full-time employees.
pj92: Money paid to the real estate agency that introduced the home when you rent it.
pj93: Junior High School Graduation Equivalency Examination
An exam for people who have not graduated from a Japanese junior high school. If you pass, you can take entrance exams for Japanese high schools.
pj94: An agreement between the person renting out a home and the person renting it.
pj95: A form submitted to the city office when moving within the same city.
pj96: A form submitted to the office of your current city when moving to another city. Also submitted when leaving Japan.
pj97: A form submitted to the office of your new city after moving from another city. Also submitted when you start living in Japan.
pj98: Money that people raising a child with a disability can receive.
pj99: Special collection (payroll deduction of resident tax)
When a company pays employees' resident tax to their local city office. The company deducts the tax from your salary.
pj100: A form submitted to the authorities before climbing, with your name, address, phone number, route, etc. It helps rescue people in mountain accidents.
pj101: A hospital department that treats internal illnesses (such as colds).
pj102: Examination for Japanese University Admission for International Students (EJU)
An exam taken by students from abroad who want to study at a Japanese university.
pj103: A checkup by your local city office to see if your baby is healthy.
pj104: Certified Center for Early Childhood Education and Care (Nintei Kodomo-en)
A facility for children before elementary school that combines features of both kindergartens and nursery schools.
pj105: A checkup to see if a pregnant woman is healthy.
pj106: A system that collects money from everyone to support elderly people and people disabled by illness or injury.
pj107: A booklet given to people who join the pension system.
pj108: Days off work for which you still receive your salary.
pj109: In December, your company recalculates the income tax withheld. If too much was withheld, you get money back; if too little, you pay the company.
pj110: A person who has a contract with a staffing agency and works at another company.
pj111: A map showing dangerous areas and evacuation sites in case of a disaster.
pj112: Parenting classes for expectant mothers and fathers
Classes that teach new parents important things about giving birth and raising a baby.
pj113: A government office that helps people find jobs.
pj114: A place that introduces people who can look after your children when you have things to do.
pj115: A shop that introduces homes to people who want to rent or buy.
pj116: A place that cares for children from age 0 until elementary school while parents work. Children receive care and learn many things through play.
pj117: A place that looks after elementary school children while their parents work.
pj118: Practice evacuating safely and putting out fires in case of a disaster.
pj119: Taking steps to avoid becoming a victim of crime.
pj120: A booklet pregnant women receive from their local city office, used to record the health of the mother and baby.
pj121: A home rented from a landlord (No.9).
pj123: A school for people who did not graduate from junior high school or could not attend enough. Graduates can take high school entrance exams.
pj124: Money paid every month for a rented home.
pj126: A place for children from age 3 until elementary school. Children learn many things through play.
pj128: A booklet issued by your local city office to people with an intellectual disability.
pj129: Money you can get back later from your health insurance after paying the full cost of medical care yourself.
pj130: A thank-you payment the tenant makes to the landlord when the rental is decided.
pj131: A person who pays the rent instead if the tenant cannot pay.
pj132: A system funded by companies that helps people injured or sick because of work.
pj133: Money people aged 65 or older can receive from the National Pension.
pj134: Money people aged 65 or older can receive from Employees' Pension Insurance.
jl印鑑登録: Registering your personal seal (inkan) with the city office.
jl火災保険: Insurance that covers damage from fire.
jl義務教育: Education that children are required to receive.
jl教育委員会: A local government body in charge of schools and education.
jl公共職業安定所: The official name of Hello Work, a government job placement office.
jl住民基本台帳: The official register of residents kept by the city office.
jl住民票: A record of your address and other details kept by the city office.
jl出入国管理: Government control of people entering and leaving the country.
jl申請書: A document used to apply for something.
jl世帯主: The person who represents a household.
jl損害賠償: Paying for harm or loss caused to someone.
jl損害保険: Insurance covering damage to property, accidents, etc.
jl宅地建物取引業: The business of buying, selling, and renting land and buildings.
jl通知書: A document informing you of something.
jl手数料: Money paid for a service or procedure.
jl登録証: A card or document proving registration.
jl難民認定: Official recognition as a refugee by the government.
jl分割払い: Paying in several parts over time.
jl保育所: The official term for a nursery school.
pj1: Time off you can take from work to raise your child.
pj2: Money you can receive from Employment Insurance while you are on childcare leave.
pj3: Money the family can receive from the National Pension when a person enrolled in it dies.
pj4: Money the family can receive from Employees' Pension Insurance when a person enrolled in it dies.
pj5: A system that collects money from everyone to help people who go to a hospital or clinic for an injury or illness.
pj6: A document that shows which seal is your registered seal (jitsuin). You can get it at your city office.
pj7: A card you use to get a certificate of seal registration at your city office. You receive it when the city office registers your seal (jitsuin).
pj8: Staying in Japan after your period of stay has expired.
pj9: A person who rents out a home.
pj10: Helping people who have difficulty with daily life (eating, bathing, etc.) because of old age or a serious illness.
pj11: Time off you can take from work to care for a family member.
pj12: Money you can receive from Employment Insurance while you are on family care leave.
pj13: A school for foreign children. There are schools suited to the culture and language of each country.
pj14: A system that collects money from people aged 40 and over to help people who need nursing care.
pj15: A board used by the neighborhood association with notices from the city office and others. After reading it, pass it to the next household.
pj16: A way of paying income tax for people whose tax is not withheld or adjusted at year-end by an employer. You submit documents to your local tax office.
pj17: Money a wife can receive from the National Pension when her husband dies.
pj18: A clinic or department that treats eye diseases.
pj19: Money paid for things shared by everyone in an apartment building. It is collected from the residents.
pj20: Compulsory education school (combined elementary and junior high school)
A school that combines elementary school and junior high school.
pj21: A vehicle that takes people who are suddenly ill or injured to the hospital.
pj22: A document from your employer showing your salary for the year and the income tax withheld.
pj23: A document from your employer showing your monthly salary and the income tax withheld.
pj24: An alert that appears on TV or smartphones shortly before strong shaking from an earthquake arrives.
pj25: A specialist who gives advice on nursing care and plans how care will be provided.
pj26: A worker whose period of employment is fixed. The contract (an agreement between the company and the worker) ends within 3 years.
pj27: A clinic or department that treats injuries and performs operations.
pj28: Medical insurance for people who work at a company.
pj29: Your employer pays income tax to the government for you by deducting it from your salary.
pj30: Housing rented out by a prefecture, city, etc.
pj31: Money returned to you when your medical bills in one month are high.
pj32: Medical care system for people aged 75 and over
Medical insurance for people aged 75 and over.
pj33: Scholarship benefit for high school students
Money that high school students from low-income families can receive to buy textbooks and study materials.
pj34: Money paid in addition to rent when you renew your lease and stay in the same home.
pj35: A pension for people up to age 69 who work at least a set number of hours at a company, factory, shop, etc.
pj36: An exam for people who did not graduate from a Japanese high school. If you pass, you can take entrance exams for universities, vocational schools, etc.
pj37: High school tuition that the government pays for you.
pj38: Medical insurance that people not covered by an employer's health insurance join themselves.
pj39: The national pension that everyone aged 20 to 59 must join.
pj40: A tax paid by people who own land or buildings.
pj41: A system that helps people who cannot find work after leaving a job, and people on childcare or family care leave.
pj42: A form that people getting married submit to their city office.
pj43: Certificate of legal capacity to marry
A document foreign nationals need when submitting a marriage registration to the city office.
pj44: The lowest wage set by law.
pj45: A card issued by immigration to foreign nationals living in Japan for more than 3 months. It shows your name, nationality, address, etc.
pj46: Permission to extend period of stay
Permission you get when you want to extend your period of stay. Your status of residence does not change.
pj47: The last day a foreign national can stay in Japan.
pj48: What a foreign national is allowed to do in Japan, such as work, attend school, or live with family.
pj49: Permission to acquire status of residence
Getting a residence card for a foreign baby born in Japan.
pj50: Permission to change status of residence
Permission you get when you change your status of residence.
pj51: Working more than 8 hours a day, or more than 40 hours a week.
pj52: Leave a working woman can take before giving birth, and leave she must take after giving birth.
pj53: A clinic or department that treats women's illnesses and helps with childbirth.
pj55: Permission to engage in activity other than that permitted
Permission needed when a person whose status of residence does not allow work wants to work.
pj56: Money paid when renting a home. After the tenant moves out, the landlord uses it to repair damage or clean the home, etc.
pj57: A group formed by people living nearby. Members work together to make the area safe and pleasant to live in.
pj58: A personal seal registered with your city office. It is used when buying a car or a house, etc.
pj59: A tax paid at the time of vehicle inspection, etc.
pj60: Automobile tax / light vehicle tax (environmental performance-based)
A tax paid when you buy a car.
pj61: Automobile tax / light vehicle tax (annual, by vehicle type)
A tax paid by people who own a car on April 1 each year.
pj62: Money people raising children can receive until the child finishes junior high school.
pj63: Money single parents (due to divorce, etc.) raising a child up to age 18 can receive. Single parents raising a child with a disability up to age 19 can also receive it.
pj64: A system that collects money from people who drive cars or motorcycles to help people injured in accidents.
pj65: Money the family receives from the National Pension when a person enrolled in the pension dies.
pj66: A form submitted to the city office when a family member or someone you lived with dies.
pj67: Government systems that collect money from workers and employers to help people in need.
pj68: An inspection every 1 or 2 years to check that a car or motorcycle is safe to drive.
pj69: A document you receive after the vehicle inspection is completed.
pj70: Financial help for school supplies, school lunches, etc. Parents of elementary and junior high school students with low income can receive it.
pj71: Detailed rules for working, set by the company.
pj72: A tax paid to the prefecture and city/ward by working people who had an address in Japan on January 1.
pj73: Money you can receive from health insurance when you take time off work to give birth and do not receive a salary.
pj74: A form submitted to the city office when a baby is born.
pj75: Money you can receive from health insurance, etc. when you give birth.
pj76: Money people with a disability can receive from the National Pension.
pj77: Money people with a disability can receive from Employees' Pension Insurance.
pj78: A tax paid when you buy goods or services.
pj79: A tax paid to the government on your income (such as wages from work).
pj80: A booklet issued by your city office to people with a physical disability.
dr国際交流協会: An organization that connects foreign residents with local people. It runs Japanese classes and other activities.
dr日本語教室: A class for studying Japanese. Local classes are often taught by volunteers.
drボランティア: A person who helps others without being paid.
dr見学: Going to see a class or place before joining.
dr教材費: Money for textbooks and other study materials.
dr空き待ち: Waiting for a spot to open when a class or place is full.
drチラシ: A single sheet of paper with a notice or advertisement.
dr申し込み: Telling someone that you want to join or use something.
dr面談: Meeting someone in person to talk.
dr集会室: A room where people gather for discussions or activities.
dr長机: A long, wide table that several people use side by side.
dr利用者登録: Registering your name and details before using a facility. Some places require it before booking a room.
dr団体登録: Registering your group in advance so the group can use a facility.
dr持ち寄り: Everyone brings a little food or other items to share.
dr利用者カード: A card used to borrow books and other items at the library.
dr貸出: Lending books and other items. Used when you borrow books at a library.
dr返却期限: The last day by which you must return something you borrowed.
dr返却ポスト: A box for returning borrowed books. It can often be used when the library is closed.
dr延長: Making a set time or date longer. At a library, it means moving the due date later.
dr館内閲覧: Reading only inside the library; you cannot take it home.
dr最新号: The newest issue of a magazine or similar publication.
dr速達: A postal service that delivers mail faster. It costs more than regular mail.
dr書留: A postal service that keeps a record of sending. It costs more than regular mail.
dr国際郵便: Mail sent to or received from another country.
dr不在連絡票: A slip left when mail could not be delivered because you were out. Use it to request redelivery.
dr再配達: Having undelivered mail or a package delivered again.
dr席を外しております: The person is not at their desk right now. Wait a moment or call again later.
drあいにく: Means "I'm sorry, but." It is followed by something that cannot be done or is not allowed.
dr申し訳ございません: A polite way to say "sorry" or "excuse me."
drお手数ですが: Means "I know it's a bother, but please." It is followed by something they want you to do.
dr差し支えなければ: Means "if it's okay." You don't have to answer if you don't want to.
drご用件: Why you called or came. Say your business briefly.
drよろしいでしょうか: A polite way to say "Is that OK?" Answer "hai" (yes) if it is.
drお伺いします: A polite way to say "ask" or "go/visit."
dr失礼いたします: A polite greeting used when hanging up the phone, entering a room, and so on.
drお越しください: A polite way to say "please come."
drお持ちください: A polite way to say "please bring."
drご記入ください: A polite way to say "please write it on the form."
drご本人様: The person in question, not a family member or someone else. That person must come or speak.
drフルネーム: Your complete name, both family name and given name.
dr日中つながる: Able to answer the phone during the daytime. Give a number you can answer then.
drご連絡先: Your phone number, email address, etc., so they can contact you.
drお手元: Something near you or that you have with you now.
dr控え: A paper with the same content as the document you submitted. Keep it yourself.
dr窓口: The place at a government office or company for consultations and procedures.
dr担当の者: The person who handles that matter. They will speak with you instead.
drお預かりします: Means "I'll hold this for a while." Hand over your documents or money.
dr原本: The original, real document, not a copy.
dr最短: In the fastest or shortest case.
dr空き: There is still room in a booking, place, etc.
drお申し込み: Requesting a service and completing the procedure to use it.
drハラール: Food and drink permitted under Islamic law.
dr揚げ油: Oil used for deep-frying foods like tempura. Many restaurants use the same oil for other dishes.
dr染み抜き: Removing stains from clothes. There is often an extra charge on top of the regular price.
drデラックス: A course with more careful finishing than usual. There is often an extra charge on top of the regular price.
dr仕上がり: When dry cleaning is finished and your clothes are ready. The "ready date" is the day you can pick them up.
drワイシャツ: A shirt with a collar and buttons, worn for work and similar occasions.
drハンガー仕上げ: Cleaned clothes are returned on a hanger.
dr引換券: A slip you show when picking up your clothes. Do not lose it.
dr会員カード: A card for store members. It may be used for points or discounts.
dr海外送金: Sending money to a person or bank in another country.
dr外国送金依頼書: A form you submit to the bank when sending money abroad. You write the recipient's name, bank, and other details.
drSWIFTコード: A code for each bank, used when sending money abroad. It is good to ask your family for it in advance.
drマイナンバー: A number given to each person living in Japan. It is used for tax and other procedures.
dr中継銀行: A bank in between when sending money abroad. It may charge a fee.
dr受取人: The person who receives money or items.
dr特急: A very fast train that skips some stations. You often need a limited express ticket in addition to a basic fare ticket.
dr快速: A train faster than a local train. It skips some stations.
dr乗車券: A ticket for riding a train.
dr特急券: A ticket you buy in addition to the basic fare ticket to ride a limited express.
dr指定席: A seat assigned to you. The seat number is printed on the ticket.
dr自由席: Seats with no assignment. You can sit in any empty seat.
dr乗り換え: Changing to another train partway. For mobile phones, it also means switching to another carrier.
dr振替輸送: When trains stop running, you can use other trains or buses instead.
drフロント: The reception desk of a hotel.
dr手配: Preparing what is needed. Arranging a taxi means calling a taxi.
dr正面玄関: The largest entrance at the front of a building.
dr迎車: A taxi coming to where the customer is. There may be a pickup fee.
drワゴン: A large vehicle that holds many people or a lot of luggage.
drクレジットカード: A card that lets you pay later all at once. Whether it can be used depends on the place.
dr運転免許更新センター: A place where you renew your driver's license.
dr更新のお知らせ: A postcard telling you your license will expire soon. When you get it, go to renew within the set period.
dr有効期限: The last day something can be used. After this date, it cannot be used.
dr講習区分: The type of lecture you take when renewing your license. Time and fees differ by type.
dr優良運転者講習: A lecture for safe drivers with no accidents or traffic violations.
dr一般講習: The standard lecture for license renewal, taken by those who are not excellent drivers, among others.
dr適性検査: A test to check if you can drive, such as an eyesight test. Bring your glasses if you use them.
dr住民票の写し: A document showing your address, name, and more. You can get it at your local city office.
drAT限定: A license for automatic cars only. You cannot drive manual cars.
drマニュアル: A car where you change gears yourself. To drive one, get a license without the AT-only restriction.
dr普通車: A normal-sized car. You can drive it with a regular driver's license.
dr教習: Learning to drive at a driving school.
dr短期プラン: A course where you take lessons continuously and graduate in a short time.
dr送迎バス: A bus that takes people between places like the station and the driving school.
dr技能検定: A test at the driving school to check if you can drive properly.
dr任意保険: Car insurance where you choose the company and coverage. It covers what compulsory insurance (jibaiseki) does not.
dr型式: Letters or numbers showing the car model. It is on the vehicle inspection certificate.
dr登録番号: The number on the car's license plate.
dr納車: Receiving the car you bought from the dealer.
dr妊婦健診: Checkups at a hospital for pregnant women, checking the health of mother and baby.
dr受診票: A form you give to the hospital for a checkup. You get it from your city or town, which pays part of the cost.
dr補助券: A slip for which your city or town pays part of the cost. For checkups, it means the checkup voucher.
dr妊娠週数: How many weeks pregnant you are, counted from the first day of your last period.
dr在留資格取得: Getting a new status to live in Japan. For a foreign child born in Japan, apply at immigration.
dr出生届受理証明書: Certificate of acceptance of birth registration
A document showing the city office accepted the baby's birth registration. You get it at the city office.
dr大使館: Your country's government office in Japan. It handles passports and other procedures.
dr乳幼児健診: Checkups for babies and young children on their health and growth.
dr月齢: How many months old a baby is.
dr医療証: A certificate for city or town support with children's medical costs. Show it at the hospital reception.
dr自費: Paying the full cost yourself without insurance or local support.
dr保育課: A section at the city office that handles daycare applications and more.
dr入園申請: Applying to enter daycare and similar facilities. Usually submitted at the city or town office.
dr申込書: A form you fill out and submit when applying for something.
dr就労証明書: A document showing that you work. Your employer fills it out.
dr締め切り: The last day you can submit documents. Submit by this day.
dr一次募集: The first application period. There may be a second round afterward.
dr途中入園: Entering daycare partway through the year, not in April.
dr学務課: A section of the board of education that handles school enrollment and more.
dr日本語学級: A classroom at school for studying Japanese, where some lessons are taken. Also called an international classroom.
dr日本語支援: Help at school for children who don't yet understand Japanese well.
dr支援員: A person who comes to school to help children with studies and more.
dr就学時健康診断: A health check for children entering elementary school next year, usually at the school they will attend.
dr上履き: Shoes worn inside school and other buildings.
dr養護教諭: The teacher in the school health room who handles children's injuries, illness, and health.
dr就学相談: Discussing with the board of education which school or class suits your child. Parents' opinions are considered.
dr聴力: The ability to hear sounds. Checkups test whether you hear well.
dr給食費: Money parents pay for school lunches.
dr引き落とし: Money paid automatically from your bank account. Keep enough money in the account.
dr届け出印: The personal seal (hanko) registered with the bank when opening an account. Also called a bank seal.
dr進路相談: Talking with teachers about your future, such as which high school to attend after junior high.
dr三者面談: A meeting between the homeroom teacher, a parent, and the student. In the 3rd year of junior high, it is used to discuss the student's future path.
dr担任: The teacher in charge of a class.
dr通訳: Translating spoken words between people who speak different languages. Also refers to the person who does this job.
dr高校進学: Finishing junior high school and entering high school. There is often an entrance exam.
dr放課後: The time after all classes for the day have finished.
dr折り返し: When the other person calls you again later. You hang up and wait.
dr特別支援学級: A class inside an elementary or junior high school for children who need extra support due to physical, mental, or learning needs.
dr特別支援学校: A school for children who need extra support due to physical, mental, or learning needs.
dr通級による指導: Studying in a regular class while receiving special instruction separately for part of the time.
dr特別支援教育コーディネーター: A school teacher who gives advice about children needing extra support and connects teachers and parents.
dr求職申込み: Registering at Hello Work (the Public Employment Security Office) to look for a job. This is often the first step.
dr求人票: A sheet from a company looking for workers, showing the job duties, hours, pay, and so on.
dr紹介状: A document from the office that introduces you to a company. Some jobs require it before you can apply.
dr就職説明会: An event where companies explain their jobs to people who are looking for work.
dr履歴書: A form where you write your name, address, education, and work experience. You submit it when applying for a job.
dr職業相談: Talking with office staff about job hunting or finding work. It is free.
drパート: Working shorter hours than full-time employees. Usually paid by the hour.
drアルバイト: Working for short hours or a short period. Usually paid by the hour.
dr派遣: Signing a contract with a staffing agency and working at another company.
dr求人: When a company or organization is looking for workers.
dr時給: The money you get for one hour of work.
dr営業部: The group in a company that sells products or services.
dr人身事故: An accident where a train or similar hits a person, causing injury or death. Trains may stop or be delayed.
dr運転見合わせ: When trains or buses are stopped and not running for a while.
dr遅延証明書: A paper showing that a train was late. Often available at the station or on the railway company's website.
dr出社: Going to the company to work.
dr総務部: The group in a company that handles company-wide work such as documents, buildings, and staff matters.
dr内線: A phone line used only within the same company or building.
dr席を外しています: He/She is away from the desk
The person is not near their desk right now. They are away for a short time.
dr会議中: The person is in a meeting now and cannot take the call.
dr戻る: To come back to the original place.
drかけ直す: To hang up and call again later.
drお疲れさまです: A greeting used between coworkers. On internal calls, people often say it before giving their name.
dr納品: Delivering ordered goods to the customer.
dr注文書: A document stating what you want to buy and how many.
dr出荷: Sending goods out from a company or warehouse to customers.
dr数量: The number or amount of something.
dr先方: The other person or the other company.
dr経緯: The sequence of how something happened and how it turned out.
dr光回線: A fast line for using the internet at home. Installation work is often needed.
drプロバイダー: A company that provides internet connection. Sometimes you sign a separate contract from the line company.
dr開通工事: Work at your home to connect the line so you can use the internet. You often need to be home.
dr解約金: Money you pay if you cancel a contract before the agreed period ends.
drホームルーター: A device that gives you internet just by plugging it into a wall outlet.
drプラン: A combination of fees and available services.
drデータ容量: The amount of internet you can use on your smartphone per month.
drかけ放題: A service where you pay a set fee and the price doesn't change no matter how many calls you make.
drオプション: An extra service you can add to a plan. It often costs money after the free period ends.
dr補償サービス: A service that helps when your smartphone is broken or lost.
dr本人確認書類: A card or similar that shows who you are. Foreign residents often show their residence card.
dr担当: The person who handles that work.
dr伝言: Asking someone to pass on what you want to say to a person who is not there. Briefly give your name, phone number, and reason.
dr承ります: A polite way of saying "I'll listen" or "I'll accept." Please say what you want to pass on.
dr外出: The person is out for work or other reasons and is not here now.
dr席を外して: The person is not nearby for a short time. You can leave a message or call back later.
dr復唱: Saying what you heard again to confirm it. Listen carefully to check for mistakes.
dr少々お待ちください: Means "Please wait a little." Stay on the line without hanging up.
drお待たせいたしました: Means "Sorry for making you wait." The conversation will continue.
dr恐れ入りますが: Means "Sorry, but…" A request or question follows.
drかしこまりました: A polite way of saying "I understand."
dr承知いたしました: A polite way of saying "I understand."
drお掛け直しください: Means "Please call again." Hang up and call back later.
dr在学証明書: A document from a school stating that the person is a student there.
dr転入学通知書: A document notifying entry into a new school. Get it from the city office (Board of Education) and submit it to the new school.
dr総合案内: A reception desk near the entrance of the city office. They tell you which counter to go to.
dr転入: Moving from another city or town. You must notify the city office within the set period.
dr保険年金課: The division at the city office that handles National Health Insurance and National Pension. The name varies by municipality.
dr番号札: A paper with a number on it. Take one at the counter and wait until your number is called.
dr納付書: A slip used to pay taxes or insurance premiums. Pay at a bank, city office counter, or convenience store.
dr普通徴収: A way of paying resident tax yourself with payment slips instead of having it deducted from your salary.
dr届出印: The seal (hanko) you registered when opening a bank account.
dr税務課: The division at the city office that handles taxes.
dr環境衛生課: A division of the city office. It handles things like dog registration.
dr犬の登録: Notifying your city or town when you start keeping a dog. Required by law, usually once in the dog's life.
dr狂犬病: A very dangerous disease transmitted by dogs and other animals. Dogs get a vaccination every year.
dr予防注射: A shot to prevent disease. Dogs get a rabies vaccination every year.
dr注射済証: Proof that the dog received a rabies vaccination. It is attached to the dog.
dr鑑札: A tag you receive when you register your dog. It is attached to the dog.
dr資格喪失証明書: Certificate of loss of insurance coverage
A document showing the date your health insurance from your previous employer ended.
